findings.title: Regenerating into user storage leaves an older local recovery-code credential active
findings.body: When a federated user previously had recovery codes stored locally (for example, while its user-storage provider did not support this credential type), and the provider later accepts updateCredential, this branch writes the new codes to user storage but does not delete the existing local recovery-code credential. The code now intentionally considers both sources (getCredential falls back to local storage), and credential validation/future provider configuration changes can therefore make the superseded local recovery codes usable again. Recovery-code regeneration must revoke all prior codes; remove or replace the local credential when creation in user storage succeeds.

findings.title: The added user-storage recovery-code implementation does not consume successful codes
findings.body: isValid returns true when a submitted code is present in the stored list but never removes or marks that code as used. Recovery authentication codes are one-time credentials, so the same code can be replayed indefinitely in the newly added integration fixture. Consequently, the new login test only proves initial validation and cannot catch regressions in code consumption or exhausted-code handling; the fixture should update its stored recovery-code state after a successful validation and the test should verify that a used code is rejected.
